Subject:       Response to Second Request for Additional Information Regarding Emergency
               License Amendment Request: One-Time-Use Amendment to Allow Alternative
               Fuel Handling Method for the Recovery of Fuel Assembly DD41


By letter dated September 30, 2026 (Reference 1), in accordance with Title 10 of the Code of
Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 50.90, Application for amendment of license, construction permit,
or early site permit and 10 CFR 50.91, Notice for public comment; State consultation, Palisades
Energy, LLC (Palisades Energy) requested U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)
approval of a one-time emergency change to the Renewed Facility Operating License (RFOL)
for Palisades Nuclear Plant (PNP). The proposed License Amendment Request (LAR) would
revise UFSAR Sections 9.11 Fuel Handling and Storage Systems, and 14.19 Fuel Handling
Accident, to facilitate transport of fuel assembly DD41 from the reactor utilizing different plant
equipment and following a different travel path than is described in the Updated Final Safety
Analysis Report (UFSAR).
On October 1, 2026, the NRC and Palisades Energy conducted a conference call in which the
NRC staff verbally and visually requested information in the form of questions related to the
proposed LAR. On October 2, 2026, a follow-up conference call was conducted between the
NRC and Palisades Energy. The purpose of the call was to provide verbal responses to the
questions raised and to identify responses required to be docketed. Palisades Energy provided
the responses to the request for additional information (RAI) in a letter dated October 2, 2026
(Reference 2).
By electronic mail (email) received on October 7, 2026, the NRC provided a second RAI
regarding the LAR.
The enclosure to this letter provides Palisades Energy’s responses to the second RAI received
by email on October 7, 2026.

This letter contains no new regulatory commitments and no revisions to existing regulatory
commitments.
In accordance with 10 CFR 50.91(b), State consultation, Palisades Energy is notifying the State
of Michigan of the revised RAI response by transmitting a copy of this letter, with Enclosure, to
the designated State of Michigan official.
If you have any questions regarding this submittal, please contact Kyle Steffic, Regulatory
Assurance Manager, at (269) 290-8915.

                             Response to Request for Information
Background:
By letter dated September 30, 2026 (Reference 1 of cover letter), in accordance with Title 10 of
the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 50.90, Application for amendment of license,
construction permit, or early site permit and 10 CFR 50.91, Notice for public comment; State
consultation, Palisades Energy, LLC (Palisades Energy) requested U.S. Nuclear Regulatory
Commission (NRC) approval of a one-time emergency change to the Renewed Facility
Operating License (RFOL) for Palisades Nuclear Plant (PNP). The proposed License
Amendment Request (LAR) would revise UFSAR Sections 9.11 Fuel Handling and Storage
Systems, and 14.19 Fuel Handling Accident, to facilitate transport of fuel assembly DD41 from
the reactor utilizing different plant equipment and following a different travel path than is
described in the Updated Final Safety Analysis Report (UFSAR).
On October 1, 2026, the NRC and Palisades Energy conducted a conference call in which the
NRC staff verbally and visually requested information in the form of questions related to the
proposed LAR. On October 2, 2026, a follow-up conference call was conducted between the
NRC and Palisades Energy. The purpose of the call was to provide verbal responses to the
questions raised and to identify responses required to be docketed. Palisades Energy provided
the responses to the request for additional information (RAI) in a letter dated October 2, 2026
(Reference 2 of cover letter).
By electronic mail (email) received on October 7, 2026, the NRC provided a second RAI
regarding the LAR. Each RAI is presented below in bold type and is followed by the Palisades
Energy response.
RAI-1
Is there an analysis of a cask drop over the spent fuel pool? If so, does the cask drop
over the spent fuel pool bound a drop of DD41 (in the FTC) onto the fuel. Please
supplement the LAR to include a section discussing how a hypothetical drop of the Fuel
Transfer Canister onto spent fuel in the spent fuel pool is bounded by existing analysis.
Response:
Yes, there is an existing analysis for the radiological consequences of a cask drop in the Spent
Fuel Pool (SFP). That analysis is UFSAR Chapter 14.11 Reference 15, NAI-1149-026, Revision
0 “Palisades Design Basis Cask Drop Analysis AST Radiological Analysis”. In section 3.1, the
analysis assumes damage to all the fuel pins in 73 fuel assemblies with a source term
representing activities for 73 fuel assemblies. Since the DD41 Fuel Transfer Canister (FTC) is
not physically large enough to impact more than 73 fuel assemblies located in their SFP storage
cells, the cask drop event evaluated in NAI-1149-026 bounds the drop of the DD41 FTC in the
SFP. Note that an FTC drop does not need to be postulated for the FTC transfer evolution due
to the fact the Spent Fuel Building Crane (L-3) will be used in a single-failure proof configuration
while handling the FTC.
 PNP 2026-055
Page 3 of 3


RAI-2
Section 9.11.4.3 (Item 6) of the FSAR indicates, “The Fuel Building Crane may be
operated in a non-single failure proof manner following site-specific heavy load
requirements. Non-single failure proof modes of operation typically involve trolley and
bridge speed increases and multiple direction movement control, and are only used
when single failure proof operation is not required. Section 14.11 describes postulated
cask drop accidents.” Section 14.11.1 of FSAR indicates “In these situations, the crane
no longer meets single failure proof requirements, and load drops are postulated.” Since
fuel transfer canister will be travelling over spent fuel within the fuel building and load
drop analysis has not been performed, confirm FB crane is operated in single failure
proof manner. In event the crane is not handled in single failure proof manner, is an
impact limiting pad required as indicated in Section 14.11.2.3.1 of FSAR?
Response:
L-3 is currently configured to be single-failure proof via implementation of Temporary
Modification (TMOD) EC-93373 in December 2024. The TMOD was installed to support the last
dry fuel loading campaign. The TMOD will remain installed until after DD41 is recovered in order
to have L-3 configured as single-failure proof while handling DD41 and the Fuel Transfer
Canister.
RAI-3
NRC staff understands that fuel assembly DD41 exhibits significant bowing. Based on
the fuel transfer canister (FTC) drawings made available on the portal, it does not appear
that the FTC design accommodates this degree of bowing. Once DD41 is placed in the
FTC, will measurements be taken to confirm the actual extent of bowing? The staff’s
concern is that when the FTC lid is installed, any existing bowing will be essentially
forced into a straighter configuration, which could result in additional damage to the
assembly and/or fuel rods. Please describe what evaluations or controls have been
implemented to ensure that no further damage will occur when DD41 is enclosed in the
FTC. Additionally, are contingency actions established in the event that the assembly is
adversely affected when the FTC lid is secured?
Response:
Once DD41 is placed on the FTC pedestals, the extent of plastic deformation and overall
assembly alignment will be confirmed using cameras before lowering the canister lid.
Based on a review by our fuel vendor, the assembly is expected to straighten out without risk of
fuel cladding failure inside the FTC. As the guide bars begin to straighten during lowering of the
lid, some axial tension and compression will be experienced at grid-to-guide bar welds, which
may ultimately result in the distortion of grid cells. As long as the fuel rods remain within the
envelope defined by the inner surface of the FTC lid, there is no potential for fuel rod failure
during lowering of the lid.
Contingency actions are captured by the site's ALARA plan. This plan includes water chemistry
sampling and radiological measurements promptly after the lid is lowered and stop work criteria
for adverse conditions identified.
